title: Diagnose a Simulated Cooling Incident
summary: Integrate thermal telemetry, airflow, capacity, redundancy, safety, and documentation.
objectives: Document evidence, uncertainty, and safe escalation without industrial service.

vocab.def: A modeled area with related environmental conditions.
Passing a concern to an authorized person or team.
Information that supports or tests an explanation.

sections.heading: Scenario packet
sections.body: Use rack temperatures, environmental trends, airflow diagram, cooling-unit status, redundancy state, high-density compute context, alarms, and recent change notes. Not every clue is causal.

sections.heading: Professional boundary
sections.body: This is simulation only. Do not open live units, handle refrigerant, service compressors, pumps, fans, chillers, electrical HVAC systems, or modify building controls. Stop and escalate.

practice.prompt: A simulated high-density rack is warming while one cooling unit is unavailable. What should the report contain?
practice.answer: Observed readings, relevant trend evidence, affected thermal zone, redundancy status, uncertainty, and safe authorized escalation.

quiz.question: What is the correct response to a simulated request to service a chiller?
options: Stop, document, and escalate to a qualified professional
quiz.answer: Stop, document, and escalate to a qualified professional

criteria: Uses relevant telemetry and trend evidence
Avoids professional service and escalates safely

lab.objective: Analyze and document a synthetic cooling incident.
